chunks: From him, from several of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Sulayman, from Abu Ayyub al-Madani, from Sulayman ibn al-Ja'fari, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said:

"Do not eat the Qunburah, nor curse it, nor give it to the children to play with, for it is abundant in the glorification of Allah, and its glorification is a curse upon those who hate the Family of Muhammad."

key_terms.الْقُنْبُرَةَ: Qunburah, a type of seaweed or marine plant mentioned in hadith
key_terms.مُبْغِضِي آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ: Those who hate the Family of Muhammad

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating and playing with Qunburah according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Rida (AS) establishes a unique legal and spiritual status for the 'Qunburah' seaweed, linking its natural glorification of God to the Ahl al-Bayt. The ruling prohibits consumption and casual use (such as for children's play) while forbidding cursing, as its specific *tasbih* serves as a divine curse upon those who harbor enmity toward the Prophet's household. This reflects the Shia concept of *tasbih al-khalq* (creation's glorification), where natural phenomena actively participate in worship and reflect spiritual realities.
